### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9ffe37153c59b0b3a64c629b9fc7d4e16e144840`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9ffe37153c59b0b3a64c629b9fc7d4e16e144840` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `179a77ca83fbe5d1f45bdf31186af1f989a8f9c5` — the merge of head `783d58770850e6357437832279c56aebce407de1` into base `9ffe37153c59b0b3a64c629b9fc7d4e16e144840`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 179a77ca83fbe5d1f45bdf31186af1f989a8f9c5 && git checkout 179a77ca83fbe5d1f45bdf31186af1f989a8f9c5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9ffe37153c59b0b3a64c629b9fc7d4e16e144840 783d58770850e6357437832279c56aebce407de1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9ffe37153c59b0b3a64c629b9fc7d4e16e144840 && git merge --no-ff 783d58770850e6357437832279c56aebce407de1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9ffe37153c59b0b3a64c629b9fc7d4e16e144840
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9ffe37153c59b0b3a64c629b9fc7d4e16e144840` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `583ad09de4504b9e7adba596b701a85d2067a0d0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.ts + packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/loader-interface.ts, packages/metadata/src/index.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #37187 for card #37039. Read: the card body and its five comments (triage first touch 7137854671, claim round 1 7150624417, os-dev-report 7151625614, triage knock 7158504687, claim round 2 7179153240; no ruling and no earlier contract-review record among them), the PR body, the ten-file list, the net diff `origin/main...583ad09d` (merge base d558de0a), and the check-runs on the head. Cited code read in the tree at this head, and cloud ADR-0118 D2, which the contract cites.

Outside this record, the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`: `.changeset/37039-row-package-binding.md` (② reads its level and its two declaration lines only), `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`, `packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`.

Check-runs on the head as read at 2026-11-26T01:12Z (pushed about 01:00Z): 67 runs, 26 success, 10 skipped, 31 in progress, 0 failed. Completed green: `Lint & Repo Gates` and all eight `Lint ·` contexts, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Live E2E UI`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`. Still running, so not yet a verdict: `Test Core` 1 to 10, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` 1 to 16, `Build & E2E UI`. This record does not stand in for them; the all-green check before landing is the seat's.

### ① Derived judgments

- `@objectstack/spec/contracts` gains one export, the interface `MetadataPackageBinding`, and `IMetadataService` gains one OPTIONAL member, `listPackageBindings?(type)`. A widening of the published surface: right. No implementer of the contract and no caller breaks, and no wrapper in the tree forwards a fixed member list (every consumer of the sibling `listDiagnosed` feature-detects on the service itself).
- No accept-set change. The hunk is TypeScript interface text, no Zod schema moves, and nothing a metadata author can write is added, refused or re-read. `Metadata-protocol: none`: right.
- The two generated snapshots each gain exactly the line the new export implies: right.
- `@objectstack/metadata` gains `MetadataManager.listPackageBindings`, `DatabaseLoader.loadRowBindings` and `rowPackageIdOf`, two optional members on `MetadataLoader`, and the type export `MetadataRowBinding`. All additive: right.
- "Every existing read is unchanged" (card item 4, PR body, changeset): right for `storedRowPackageId` (`ENVIRONMENT_HISTORY_MARK` is the literal `sys_metadata` it compared before, database-loader.ts:285), for `loadManySlots` (same entries and order through `typeRowSlots`), for `list` and `listDiagnosed` (`readListKeyed` plus `listedInSlotOrder` answering keys maps back to the same values in the same order) and for `withEntryPackage` (same return, one WeakMap write). WRONG in one case: S2 below.
- The new read is uncached and walks the loaders twice. It joins no cache entry of `list`, so it cannot change what `list` serves: right.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset names `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/metadata`, the two packages the diff publishes from, both at `patch`. With `Metadata-protocol: none` the level is `patch` by AGENTS.md Post-Task item 3 ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships patch"). The level matches.
- The Clause-② line reads `yes (widening)` in the PR body, in the changeset body and on both claims, line-initial in the first two. It matches the diff: a new optional member and a new export on a published contract, nothing removed or tightened.
- `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in the os-dev-report: empty. Nothing to answer.
- The report's out-of-scope finding, repeated as the PR's first acceptance note (`list` lists a stored row twice when its body's stamp differs from its column): confirmed by reading, and it predates this diff. The registry keys the primed copy by the body's stamp (`storeWriteKey`), `admitLoaderSlots` admits the row under the column's slot, and neither shadows the other. This diff does not change it; the new read inherits it and answers both entries with the same name, the same column and `source: 'row'`. It deserves a card, because the first consumer of the new read (cloud#4973) will receive two entries for one row and must not count them as two skills. Not blocking here. The carrier is the seat, as the note says.
- The PR's second acceptance note (a legacy row the boot pass binds "can answer that package as its column" after a boot): not true on the boot that does the binding. See S1.
- The four derived gates the dev could not measure locally (exit 3): answered by CI, not by this record. Their lint families are green on this head; the build and test families were still running when read.
- Security: no `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**`, so the path-based label instruction does not apply. The `yes` on the line above is meant, narrowly: the contract hunk teaches a trust rule (a body's package stamp is what the row's author wrote; a consumer that gates on the binding reads the column and treats a degraded answer as unknown), and cloud ADR-0118 D2 uses that binding to decide which skills load and under which tool allow-set. No permission, credential, token or authentication code changes. Whether that earns the `security` label is the seat's call.
- Rule change: no path under `.claude/**`, and the PR body declares no `Rule-change:` line. None.
- SQL push-down: no finding. `loadRowBindings` reuses `readTypeRows`, the one type-wide query `loadManySlots` already issues, with the same filter and the same cache entry. It materialises no new id set. The match of rows to listed items is against the in-memory registry, which SQL cannot see, so there is no in-app join that could push down.
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. No off-relay author to name.
- File surface: the ten files of the diff are exactly the round-2 claim's surface. No `docs/adr/**`, no `skills/**`.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.ts` (hits).** The contract choice holds. A sibling member keeps `list` and `query` byte-identical, which is card item 4, and optional-like-`listDiagnosed` is the right shape for a member only a row-backed service can answer; the text forbids substituting `list`. Against cloud ADR-0118 D2: D2 has the registry read the binding "as the protocol states it, which for a record the write door saved is derived from the row's package column", says a skill bound to no package does not load, and says the `sys_metadata` sentinel names none. The contract's two arms, its `null` for an empty column and the sentinel reading `null` (`storedRowColumnPackageId`) agree with all three, and `null` is the fail-closed direction for that consumer. Against the card: items 1 to 3 are each a sentence of the jsdoc, and `source` is the mark item 3 asks for. The contract as written is sound; what follows is where the code does not yet meet it.

**Implementing files, against the contract sentence by sentence.**

S1 (should-fix) — `listPackageBindings` answers the column as it was READ, and the boot priming pass rewrites that column after the read. `DatabaseLoader.handOut` records `rowPackageId` on the copy it hands out (database-loader.ts:1303). The pass registers that copy with `skipSourceLoader`, `register` calls `bindReadRowPackage` (metadata-manager.ts:1385-1386), and for a legacy row whose body names its own `packageId` that method writes `package_id` (database-loader.ts:1354) and never touches `readRowColumns`. `listPackageBindings` asks the identity path first (metadata-manager.ts:1858-1859), so for the rest of that process the item answers `packageId: null, source: 'row'` while its row's column holds the package. The key path one line below would read the fresh column and is never reached. The next boot answers the package. The scenario is the existing test `[R7-A] an agent legacy row` (database-loader.test.ts:1998) followed by one `listPackageBindings('agent')`; no test in the diff covers it. This contradicts the contract sentence "an item a stored row holds answers `source: 'row'` and that row's column", and it makes the PR's acceptance note for cloud#4973 true only from the boot after the binding one. The error is fail-closed under ADR-0118 D2 (bound to none, so not loaded), which is why it is not graded higher; but the answer changes across a restart with no write in between, and a consumer cannot tell. Fix shape: record the bound column on the handed-out item when `bindReadRowPackage` writes it, or resolve the identity path against the row as it stands, and pin it with the R7-A scenario.

S2 (should-fix) — `readTypeRows` now throws on a row that `main` serves. `this.readRowColumns.set(data, ...)` (database-loader.ts:1259) runs on whatever `rowToData` returns, and `rowToData` returns a JSON primitive unchanged (`applyConversionsToStoredItem` returns a non-object as it is, packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts:127). A WeakMap refuses a non-object key with a TypeError. It is thrown inside the `try`, `rethrowUnlessTableUnprovisioned` rethrows it, and the whole type's plural read fails: `loadMany`, `loadManyKeyed` and `loadManySlots`, so `list` answers degraded with none of that loader's rows of the type and the boot pass primes none of them. On `main` the same row (a `metadata` column holding `5`, `true` or a double-encoded string) is pushed and handed out as a spread copy, and every other row of the type is served. No writer in this tree stores such a body (`register` refuses a non-document), and an unparseable column already fails the read on `main`, so the exposure is a hand-written or corrupted row. But card item 4, the PR body and the changeset all promise the existing reads unchanged, and after this diff one such row costs the whole type, `object` included. Fix shape: set the entry only when `data` is an object. One line, plus a pin.

N1 (nit) — the contract says a row loader that could not be read "leaves items it holds answering `'registration'`" (metadata-service.ts:459-460). The registry's primed copies of that loader's rows still answer `'row'` by identity, as the PR's fifth test pins. The sentence is safe to act on, since a degraded answer is unknown either way, but it says more than the code does.

N2 (nit) — a `datasource:` loader that does not implement the optional `loadRowBindings` has its rows answered `'registration'` with `degraded: false`. `DatabaseLoader` is the only `datasource:` loader in the tree, so nothing reaches this today. A follow-up card could have the manager report such a loader as unread.

N3 (nit) — when both walks lose the same loader, `errors` names it twice and `reportLoaderReadFailure` fires twice for one read.

N4 (nit) — `rowColumns.get(key)!` (metadata-manager.ts:1860) asserts away `null`, a legal value there. The runtime value is right; the type is narrower than the value.

N5 (nit) — "and nowhere else" (metadata-service.ts:445) reads broader than the member's own second arm, which binds an item with no row by its registration.

The nits may ride the head that closes S1 and S2, or stand as accepted deviations. None changes a verdict.

**Break attempts that held.**

- Key agreement: `rowColumns` is keyed by the same expression `admitLoaderSlots` uses (`storeSlotKey` over the served body and `entry.packageId`, else the body's package), and by `entry.name` for the other types, as `admitLoaderItems` does. First row of a key wins on both sides, in the same loader order.
- A registry item the pass primed from a FILE while a stored row shares its key: no identity entry, so the key path answers the row's fresh column. Right.
- A `withEntryPackage` stamped copy: traced to its origin through `stampedCopyOrigins`, so a row bound by its column alone still answers by identity.
- A customization row held for a package (`pluralEntryCustomizedHolders`): keyed under the holder's slot, answers its own empty column, `null`. Literal to the contract.
- A code registration whose key a legacy row shares answers `'row'` and the row's column, `null` for an empty one: the manager's stated rule, fail-closed.
- `in its order`: both reads go through `readListKeyed` and `listedInSlotOrder`; bundled types keep the slot-first order.
- Ambiguous-stem errors still throw out of the new read, as out of `list`.
- `loader-interface.ts` and `index.ts`: the two optional members and the export say what `DatabaseLoader` does, except that `rowPackageIdOf` is the column as read (S1).

Nothing here is graded above should-fix. S1 and S2 are open on this head and each owes a delta review of its fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-olnt1r`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbXcTgn3UMemcSRTDMs`

Independence pair: the review was rendered by an isolated sub-agent served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, whose inputs were the card, the PR and the head's check-runs, and not the dispatching seat's conclusions. `session_01JQwxbXcTgn3UMemcSRTDMs` adopts and posts it. The diff was produced on branch `claude/project-thread-olnt1r`.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `783d58770850e6357437832279c56aebce407de1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.ts + packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/loader-interface.ts, packages/metadata/src/index.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Delta review of PR #37187 for card #37039, by the reviewer of the round-1 record on head `583ad09d` (PR comment 7179564385), which left S1 and S2 open. Read this round: the card body and its five comments (unchanged since round 1; no ruling, no record), the PR body (its declaration lines, test section and acceptance notes read as in round 1) and its ten-file list (the same ten paths), the delta `git diff 583ad09d 783d5877` (commits 233d98b2 and 783d5877; five files, 67 insertions, 10 deletions), the net diff against `main` where the delta touches it (merge base still d558de0a), and the check-runs on this head. The hunks the delta does not touch are as the round-1 record judged them.

S1: closed
S2: closed

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Outside this record, the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`: `.changeset/37039-row-package-binding.md` (② reads its level and its two declaration lines only), `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`, `packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`.

Check-runs on the head as read at 2026-11-26T01:25Z (CI had just started): 37 runs so far, 12 success, 9 skipped, 16 in progress, 0 failed. Completed green: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`. Still running, so not yet a verdict: the other six `Lint ·` contexts, all four `Type Check ·` contexts, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Live E2E UI`, and the two shard plans; the `Test Core` and `Test UI` shards had not been created yet. This record does not stand in for them; the all-green check before landing is the seat's.

### ① Derived judgments

- The delta adds no export, no member and no signature. In `packages/spec` it changes jsdoc text only, so the two generated snapshots owe no regeneration: right.
- In `@objectstack/metadata` it adds one private method (`DatabaseLoader.recordRowColumn`), one statement in `bindReadRowPackage`, and a typed local in `listPackageBindings`. No public surface moves: right.
- Accept-set: unchanged. `Metadata-protocol: none` still right.
- "Every existing read is unchanged", which round 1 judged wrong in one case, is now right: the WeakMap write is guarded, so `readTypeRows` treats a primitive-body row as `main` does (S2 below).
- The net diff against `main` is the same ten files (448 insertions, 15 deletions). The round-1 judgments on the published surface stand: one new export `MetadataPackageBinding`, one new optional member `listPackageBindings?`, additive members on `MetadataManager`, `DatabaseLoader` and `MetadataLoader`, the type export `MetadataRowBinding`. A widening: right.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset front matter is untouched: `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/metadata` at `patch`, which is the level `Metadata-protocol: none` takes (AGENTS.md Post-Task item 3). The delta fixes two defects inside the same unreleased addition and publishes nothing further, so the level still matches.
- The Clause-② line still reads `yes (widening)`, line-initial, in the PR body and in the changeset body, and still matches the diff.
- The one changeset sentence the delta rewrites (a legacy row whose empty column the boot pass binds answers the package the pass wrote) agrees with the code at this head. It is prose, the lane seat's.
- `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No new dev flag and no `open_questions` entry reached the card or the PR body since round 1. The round-1 answers stand, including the duplicate-listing finding (predates the diff, deserves a card, the seat carries it).
- The PR body's second acceptance note (a legacy row the boot pass binds "can answer that package as its column" after a boot), which round 1 found untrue on the binding boot, is true in the tree at this head.
- The PR body's test section still says five cases; the describe now holds seven. PR-body prose, the seat's to refresh or leave.
- Security: unchanged from round 1. No `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**`. The `yes` is meant, narrowly: the contract jsdoc, reworded in this delta, still teaches which package binding a gating consumer may trust. No permission, credential, token or authentication code changes. The label is the seat's call.
- Rule change: no path under `.claude/**`, and the PR body declares no `Rule-change:` line. None.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The delta adds no query. `bindReadRowPackage` issues the same find and the same single-row update as before.
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- File surface: the delta stays inside the round-2 claim's surface.

### ④ Design judgment

**S1, closed.** `bindReadRowPackage` now records the bound package on the handed-out item directly after the update that writes it (database-loader.ts:1367, `recordRowColumn(item, read.packageId)`), before `invalidate`. `item` is the very copy `handOut` gave the priming pass, the one `register` stores and `readRowColumnOf` asks by identity, so the identity path answers the column as the pass left it. The recorded value is exactly what the update wrote. If the update throws, nothing is recorded, which is the right order. A second call for the same item returns early and changes nothing. The fix is the first fix shape round 1 named, and it is pinned: the R7-A scenario followed by `listPackageBindings('agent')` answers the bound package with `source: 'row'`, and a fresh loader's `loadRowBindings` agrees (database-loader.test.ts:4846). The contract sentence "an item a stored row holds answers `source: 'row'` and that row's column" now holds on the binding boot.

**S2, closed.** Every write to `readRowColumns` goes through `recordRowColumn` (database-loader.ts:1314), which sets the entry only for a non-null object. The three call sites are `readTypeRows` (1259), `handOut` (1303) and the S1 line (1367); no direct `set` remains. A row whose stored body is a JSON primitive is skipped there and otherwise flows through `readTypeRows` exactly as on `main`, so the type's other rows are served. Pinned: a `skill` row whose `metadata` is `42` beside a normal row, read through `loadMany` and through `list` (database-loader.test.ts:4869). In the new read such a row has no identity entry and answers by key, its own empty or filled column, like any other listed row.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.ts` (hits), the jsdoc edits.**

- N5, closed. "never on the body's package stamp" (line 445) replaces "and nowhere else", and "a stored item's package binding" scopes the sentence to items with a row. It no longer contradicts the member's second arm.
- N1, closed. The degraded sentence now names the exception the code has: a copy the registry primed from that loader's rows still answers `'row'`. That is what `readRowColumnOf` does when `loadRowBindings` throws, and the PR's degraded test pins it.
- N6 (nit) — the same sentence says the primed copy answers "the column it was read with" (line 462). After the S1 fix a copy whose row the pass bound answers the column the pass wrote, not the one the read found. The main arm ("that row's column") and the changeset both say it correctly; this clause is one step behind. It cannot change what a consumer does, since the sentence ends by telling it to treat a degraded answer as unknown.

**`packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts`, the typing edit.**

- N4, closed. `keyedColumn` is typed `string | null | undefined` and `null` is no longer asserted away (lines 1860-1861). For every entry a typed loader can return, the answer is identical to round 1's: `rowPackageId` is `string | null`, so a held key always answers `'row'`. An entry from an untyped loader that omits `rowPackageId` now falls through to `'registration'` where it used to answer `'row'` with an undefined package. That is N2's hypothetical loader again, not a new case in the tree.

**Did the delta introduce anything new?** One residual, graded a nit.

- N7 (nit) — `bindReadRowPackage` returns early when the fresh row already holds the package (`row.package_id === read.packageId`, database-loader.ts:1337), and on that path the item keeps the `null` it was read with. Within one process this path is not reachable with a stale item: the pass reads a type once, and a read after the bind is fresh. It needs a second process to bind the row between this process's plural read and its own bind attempt, that is, two nodes on their first boot over the same unbound legacy row. The loser then answers `null` for that row until it restarts. This is outside S1, which was the deterministic single-process case, and it is fail-closed. A registry copy is in any case as old as the process's last read of its row, for the body `list` serves and for the column alike. A follow-up card could record the fresh row's column on that early return, one line.

N2 and N3 stand as round 1 left them: accepted deviations, N2 a follow-up card candidate.

- A row the pass refuses to bind (stamp-only body, another writer's `source`, a slot another row holds) returns before the update, and its copy keeps the `null` its row still holds. Right.
- The recorded value cannot be the `sys_metadata` sentinel or empty: `read.packageId` comes from `storedRowPackageId`, which admits neither.
- `rowPackageIdOf` still answers `undefined` for an object the loader did not hand out; the guard only narrows what is stored.
- `loader-interface.ts` and `index.ts` are untouched and still describe what `DatabaseLoader` does. With S1 closed, `rowPackageIdOf` no longer lags the row on the binding boot.
